A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' set-based neural-network training and verification work, despite the shortened title and substantial revision. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN, including accuracy, verification, ablation, and timing results in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR10, plus a synthetic classification example. Section V and Appendices A–C document these experiments; the separately identified literature results are not their only empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Section IV replaces v1's set-valued point-loss evaluation plus interval-norm penalty with a loss evaluated at the output-set center plus an F-radius penalty. Nonlinear backpropagation now differentiates the enclosure slopes and approximation errors instead of using only the slopes. Direct parameter gradients replace symbolic-zonotope aggregation under uniformly distributed factors, including the former 1/3 generator weighting.

E1.justification: MNIST and SVHN remain, but Fashion-MNIST clothing classification is removed and CIFAR10 natural-object classification is added. v2 also introduces a two-dimensional binary classification experiment using 20 synthetic samples in Figure 5 and Appendix B.

E2.justification: The main comparisons expand from Point and PGD to include evaluated TRADES, IBP, and SABR baselines in the accuracy and timing tables. v2 also adds literature-reported Mirman et al. results for MNIST and CIFAR10, explicitly noting different training hyperparameters. The comparison against Singh's image enclosure is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes evaluation from 500 unseen inputs to complete canonical test sets, switches SVHN networks from tanh to ReLU, and specifies additional normalization after perturbation. Training PGD changes from five to eight iterations; testing retains 40 iterations but changes the step size from epsilon_test/40 to 0.01. Added IBP and SABR comparisons use interval verification, while the other methods use zonotope verification.

E4.justification: v1's approximation-error omission and tau=0 ablations, along with comparisons across training perturbation radii, are removed. v2 adds the trained decision-boundary example in Figure 5. The enclosure case study also changes from an nn-small Fashion-MNIST network in v1 Figure 3 to an nn-med MNIST network in v2 Figure 4 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging accuracies over ten runs, and v1 already displays shaded bands in Figure 5. v2 adds numerical ± entries throughout its original accuracy tables and explicitly states ten-run averaging for the timing table. The meaning of ± remains unspecified; there is no reported increase in the number of accuracy runs.

E6.justification: The accuracy and timing results are extensively replaced, with new comparator and CIFAR10 entries and removed Fashion-MNIST and ablation entries. For example, MNIST nn-large Set verified accuracy at training and testing radius 0.1 changes from 6.18% in v1 Table 3 to 85.36±0.74% in v2 Table II. These results use the revised method and protocols and therefore do not establish a controlled performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the interval-norm and probabilistic aggregation derivations with F-radius definitions, zonotope-parameter gradients, and new chain-rule proofs for enclosure backpropagation and parameter updates in Appendix E. The enclosure-comparison theorem is retained. A new inconsistency appears: Proposition 5's 1/n normalization of the Frobenius norm does not agree with the input-radius identity in Eq. 9 or the gradient in Proposition 11.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden v1's claim of outperforming adversarial training 'in many cases' to consistently matching or outperforming state-of-the-art robust training approaches. v2 also makes the relationship to TRADES, the two additional hyperparameters, and verification using polynomial-time algorithms explicit central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a substantive explanation connecting F-radius minimization to TRADES and movement of decision boundaries, and interprets increasing MNIST verified accuracy with network size. It removes v1's discussion of memory limits, approximation-error-induced gradient distortion, and unmodified regression applicability. Appendix A adds qualifications concerning absent data augmentation, baseline implementations, and restrictions to polynomial-time verifiers.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents initialization, learning rates and decay, warm-up and ramp-up schedules, baseline-specific hyperparameters, and implementation choices in Appendix A. Appendices B and C provide the synthetic sample coordinates and training settings, plus the network run and test-image index used for the enclosure example. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the CORA implementation framework and reported hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the approach as an extension of TRADES and an alternative to robust training requiring stronger verification procedures. It adds substantive discussion and citations for SABR, branch-and-bound verification, and robust initialization. References supporting v1's symbolic-zonotope aggregation and interval-norm formulation are removed, beyond simple reference renumbering.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten and reordered, contributions become an expanded list, and the method and evaluation explanations are substantially recast. The title drops 'End-To-End,' and the appendices are reorganized from evaluation details and proofs into separately structured evaluation, reproduction, and proof sections.

P2.justification: Typography, headers, section styling, captions, and table formatting change throughout. v2 adds enclosure-step, decision-boundary, and gradient illustrations, updates the backpropagation diagram, and replots the accuracy comparisons. Accuracy tables are restructured around separate verified/falsified columns, and the timing table changes orientation and displayed configurations. Several retained figures are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis through direct comparisons with certified-training methods, full-test-set evaluation, and much fuller experimental documentation in Section V and Appendices A–C. Its expanded gradient derivations also make the revised procedure more assessable. These gains outweigh the loss of component ablations, although important weaknesses remain: inconsistent F-radius normalization, undefined ± statistics, and a headline claim of consistent competitiveness that overstates the exceptions in Table II.
